I am seventy-two years old. My back is not what it used to be, and it is just my wife and me working the land now, so I must be careful with labor. I have farmed these fields for sixty years, and I know what works in Quzhou. My well gives me reliable water, but electricity for the pump costs money, so I do not waste a drop.

This year I will keep my 6.7 mu in the wheat-maize rotation and my 3.5 mu in stevia. The wheat-maize land is my backbone: I sow wheat in mid-October, harvest it by early June, and plant maize the same day. I cannot afford to let that land sit idle. For the wheat, I will rotary-till the soil and sow the improved seed I have always used—about 30 jin per mu. I will put down 100 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as a base and another 100 kg of urea for the topdressing, spread across the three irrigations I give it: one at green-up, one at jointing, and one at flowering. I also spray for insects twice, for weeds three times, and for fungus once, because if I let the rust or the aphids in, the crop is finished. I expect around 1,100 jin per mu.

As soon as the wheat is off the field in early June, I will plant the hybrid maize without tilling—no-tillage saves my back and saves time. I will use one package of seed per mu and spread 80 kg of compound fertilizer (28-6-6) at sowing. Maize here does not need as much water as wheat, so I will irrigate twice: once right after sowing and once at the big-ear stage. Two sprays for insects and one growth regulator should be enough. If the weather cooperates, I hope for about 1,600 jin per mu.

My 3.5 mu of stevia is my cash crop. It is sown in late March and harvested in early August. I rotary-till that plot because stevia likes loose soil. I plant the Chengguang variety, about 9,333 plants per mu. It is hungry for fertilizer, so I put down 100 kg of compound (18-12-18) at planting and another 240 kg of compound (15-15-15) later in the season. I irrigate four times and spray for pests and fungus seven times each—stevia leaves must be clean to sell to the buyers. I usually get about 600 jin of dry leaves per mu.

This is the plan I have followed for years, and at my age I see no reason to change what still feeds us and pays the bills.
